articles.title: Dozens killed in rebel attacks on Sudan’s Kordofan, medical group says
articles.summary: Sudan Doctors Network says SPLM-N rebels killed 27 people in South Kordofan, including four children.
articles.body:
A medical organisation has accused a Sudanese rebel group aligned with the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) of killing 27 people, including four children, in the southern province of South Kordofan.

In a statement on Tuesday, the Sudan Doctors Network said the killings were carried out by the Sudan People's Liberation Movement (SPLM-N) in Qardud and Abu Hamama, areas inhabited by the Otoro tribe in South Kordofan.

"The attacks resulted in a large wave of displacement among citizens towards the Abu Hitan area and Kadugli," it said.

Targeting unarmed civilians on ethnic grounds constitutes a "clear violation of international humanitarian law", the group added, warning that continued violations threatened to turn "the conflict in South Kordofan into a broader ethnic conflict".

The killings follow intense fighting earlier this year between forces linked to SPLM-N and the Otoro tribe, which is a minority group in the Nuba Mountains of South Kordofan.

The ethnic standoff, first instigated by land disputes, adds another layer to the country's ongoing civil war , which broke out in April 2023 between the Sudanese army and the RSF.

The Sudan Doctors Network urged the international community to exert pressure on SPLM-N leadership to halt attacks on civilians, noting that women were also among those wounded in the latest attacks.

The SPLM-N is a breakaway faction of the SPLM, the ruling party of neighbouring South Sudan.

Its leader, Abdel Aziz al-Hilu, has aligned his fighters with the RSF and joined ranks with the RSF-led parallel government in Sudan.

The civil war in Sudan has killed at least 59,000 people and forced some 14 million people from their homes.

According to the World Health Organization, some 33.7 million people, or two-thirds of the country's population, require humanitarian assistance.

articles.title: Chinese artist Gao Zhen sentenced to 3 years in prison over satirical Mao artworks
articles.summary: Gao Zhen, who is based in the U.S., was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024 and charged over works that authorities deemed insulting to revolutionary figures.
articles.body: BANGKOK — Chinese artist Gao Zhen was sentenced to three years in prison Tuesday for “infringing upon the reputation of heroes” through his satirical works of art, including statues of China’s former leader Mao Zedong. The U.S.-based Gao, who was part of an artistic duo known internationally as the Gao Brothers, was arrested while visiting family in China in August 2024. He has been in official custody since then. He was sentenced by the Sanhei People’s Court in northern Hebei province, according to his wife, Zhao Yaliang. The charges against Gao relate to artistic works that China’s authorities deem insulting to revolutionary figures. One was a 2009 statue called “Mao’s Guilt,” which shows the former leader and founder of modern China kneeling in repentance, and another was the “Miss Mao” series of caricatures depicting Mao with breasts and an engorged nose. Shane Yi, a researcher at Chinese Human Rights Defenders, who has been advocating for Gao’s case, described the sentence as “a very clear case of a violation of a person’s freedom of expression.” Yi said the artist plans to appeal the sentence and noted that the artworks in question were created before the law Gao was sentenced with had been passed. The court did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Amnesty International criticized the court sentence, which it described as a deterrent against artistic expression. “The lengthy pretrial detention and, ultimately, decision to convict Gao Zhen and sentence him to the maximum three-year prison term under this offense illustrate the authorities’ determination to deter others from engaging in independent artistic expression,” said Amnesty’s China director, Sarah Brooks. “No artist should face criminal punishment for creating work that challenges official narratives or encourages critical reflection on history,” she said. Zhao said she hopes to be reunited with her husband and be able to return to the U.S., where the family had immigrated. “I felt two years was my limit, and I was really disappointed and sad. I haven’t been able to catch my breath,” she said. She had prepared clothes for her husband hoping that he would be released. Chinese courts often count pretrial detention as time served in a sentence. The Gao Brothers, whose works addressed themes of authoritarianism and censorship, became famous in a time of relative openness in China and were exhibited both inside the country and abroad. However, in recent years, the state has increased its controlling grip on certain aspects of expression, especially in regard to political figures with the passage of the law in 2018 that bans criticism of the nation’s heroes.

articles.title: Chinese humanoid robot that beat Usain Bolt’s 100-meter sprint record does it again, but even faster
articles.summary: The race was part of the World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition in Beijing that showcases China’s rapid advances in robotics amid growing rivalry with the U.S.
articles.body: BEIJING — A Chinese humanoid robot set a new 100-meter sprint record of 8.86 seconds in Beijing on Tuesday, beating its robot competitors — and the fastest recorded human time. The race was part of China’s World Humanoid Robot Games, an Olympic-style competition now in its second year in Beijing. The event is also a showcase for China’s rapid advances in robotics amid an intensifying technology rivalry with the U.S. The Tiangong Ultra humanoid robot beat its own record of 9.39 seconds it had set just three days earlier at the event’s opening on Saturday. For comparison, the men’s 100-meter world record is 9.58 seconds, set by Jamaican sprinter Usain Bolt in 2009. Experts are amazed to see such progress in the humanoid robot industry. “This is a significant milestone — not simply because the robot ran faster than a human, but because of what it takes to make a bipedal robot run at this speed,” said Dennis Hong, a professor of mechanical and aerospace engineering at the University of California, Los Angeles. “As speed increases, balance, control, impacts, actuator performance and mechanical robustness all become much more challenging,” Hong said. The record-breaking robot fell after hitting the finish line, a padded barrier, with sparks flying from its waist. Hong pointed out that the fall leads to more meaningful and difficult questions: whether robots can move and stop safely, recognize unexpected obstacles, recover from mistakes and continue working, the capabilities that ultimately make them more useful. The games feature over 1,300 competitions involving more than 2,000 robots in 51 events like running, long jump and table tennis, as well as ballroom dancing. Unlike the traditional Olympics, the robots also compete in teams in real-world scenarios, including household tasks, hotel services and emergency response. “’Housekeeper’ and ‘caregiver’ robots are still in the pilot and validation phase,” China’s official newspaper People’s Daily said Monday, but “challenges are precisely where the focus of development lies. … China’s robotics industry is evolving toward higher quality and innovation.”

articles.title: Assam housing push: Centre clears 3.8 lakh PMAY homes worth Rs 5,000 crore; aid for flood-hit areas
articles.summary: News News: Assamâs flood-hit families looking to rebuild could get fresh housing support, with the Centre approving new homes under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojan.
articles.body: Assamâs flood-hit families looking to rebuild could get fresh housing support, with the Centre approving new homes under the Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana and assuring additional houses for flood-affected areas.Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma said on Tuesday met Union agriculture minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who handed him the approval document for new PMAY homes involving an investment of nearly Rs 5,000 crore.Chouhan also assured Sarma that additional PMAY houses would be sanctioned for flood-affected areas, helping people rebuild at the earliest."Deeply grateful to Honâble Union Minister Shri @ChouhanShivraj Ji for the priority and support he continues to extend to Assam," the chief minister said in a post on X."In todayâs meeting, he formally handed over the approval for 3.8 lakh new homes under PM Awas Yojana, involving an investment of nearly Rs 5,000 crore", Sarma said.The Centre will also extend further support for housing in Assamâs tea garden areas, according to the chief minister.Rs 139 crore sanctioned to boost farmingHousing was not the only support discussed during the meeting. Sarma said he also received a sanction letter for Rs 139 crore under the Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana.The funds are aimed at boosting agricultural investment and promoting sustainable farming.The chief minister expressed his "sincere gratitude," on behalf of the people of Assam, to Chouhan for his swift decisions and for standing firmly with the people of the state during the recent devastating floods.What PM Awas Yojana aims to provideThe Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana was launched on June 25, 2015, by Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It aims to construct about 2 crore houses in the country from 2015 to 2022.The scheme covers homeless citizens, poor urban people and citizens belonging to the EWS and LIG categories.Its mission is to address the housing needs of the urban poor, including slum dwellers, through four programme verticals: slum rehabilitation of slum dwellers with participation from private developers using land as a resource; affordable housing for weaker sections through credit-linked subsidy; affordable housing in partnership with public and private sectors along with subsidy for beneficiary-led individual house construction.Housing needs under pressureHousing is one of the basic social conditions that determine the quality of life and welfare of people and places. Rapid urbanisation has placed considerable strain on housing, services and land.According to UN-Habitat, by 2030, approximately 3 billion people, or about 40% of the worldâs population, will need proper housing and access to basic infrastructure and services such as water and sanitation systems. This translates into the need to complete 96,150 housing units per day with serviced and documented land from now until 2030.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: Prosecutor in infamous killer mom case says women on Lindsay Clancy jury may bring ‘strange twist’ to verdict
articles.summary: Rep. Tommy Pope, who prosecuted Susan Smith, says women jurors may be less sympathetic to Lindsay Clancy's postpartum psychosis defense than expected.
articles.body: A South Carolina lawmaker who prosecuted Susan Smith in her infamous double-murder case says the women on Lindsay Clancy's jury could prove to be a "strange twist," and may be less sympathetic to her than many assume. Clancy, 36, has been charged with three counts of first-degree murder in connection with the deaths of her children — Cora, Dawson and Callan, all younger than 6 — who were discovered strangled at the family's home in January 2023. Her defense attorney says she was experiencing postpartum psychosis at the time she killed her children. LINDSAY CLANCY'S THREE CHILD VICTIMS FORGOTTEN AMID CROWDS OF SUPPORT: MOTHER OF SIX Testimony is expected to finish on Wednesday, with closing arguments anticipated for Thursday, after which the case will go to the jury. The panel seated for the trial is made up of 12 women and six men, but only 12 of them will deliberate, the rest serve as alternates and will be dismissed before deliberations begin. Smith is the South Carolina mother who was convicted of killing her two young sons, 3-year-old Michael and 14-month-old Alexander, by strapping them into her car and letting it roll into a lake. Prosecutors argued she killed them in part because the man she was romantically involved with didn't want a relationship with women who had kids. She was sentenced to life in prison. HEATED LINDSAY CLANCY COURTROOM EXCHANGE OVER 911 CALL, CRIME SCENE PHOTOS SETS STAGE FOR MOM’S MURDER TRIAL Rep. Tommy Pope, who is currently the speaker pro tempore for the South Carolina House of Representatives, prosecuted Smith and told Fox News Digital that women on the jury might be less sympathetic to Clancy than people think. "For the most part, the women were the ones that said, you know, when I had my kids, I went through hell, or I went through depression, or I battled this, or I was overwhelmed. But they're the most important thing in my life," Pope said. "And so, strange twist, while a woman may have even faced postpartum depression, she may have overcome it and then be less sympathetic to Clancy." LINDSAY CLANCY TRIAL: POSTPARTUM IS REAL, BUT CHILD KILLING DEMANDS ACCOUNTABILITY, VETERAN PROSECUTOR SAYS On the flip side, Pope said Clancy's current physical condition might complicate things for the prosecution in an unexpected way. "A weird mix, too, is having her in the courtroom, whether she intentionally injured herself or, as the prosecution said, tried to slide down and just got injured. You have somebody that's now paralyzed, which obviously doesn't equate to killing three children," Pope said. "But some jurors, and I would think maybe even more so men, would think, well, she's already punished. She's in a wheelchair. So in a strange twist, it could almost be the opposite." LINDSAY CLANCY DEFENSE SCORES ‘EXTREMELY HELPFUL’ PSYCHOSIS CONCESSION AS EXPERT FLAGS NEXT HURDLE Prosecutors on Tuesday continued to challenge the psychosis argument that Clancy's defense attorney says frees her from criminal responsibility for her children's deaths. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X LISTEN TO THE NEW 'CRIME & JUSTICE WITH DONNA ROTUNNO' PODCAST Gregory Saathoff, a forensic psychiatrist at the University of Virginia who consults for the FBI's Behavioral Analysis Unit, told jurors that Clancy's self-described auditory hallucinations were "very unusual." PROSECUTOR CORNERS LINDSAY CLANCY'S CATHOLIC MOTHER-IN-LAW WITH 'MORTAL SIN' QUESTION "What was significant to me is that she had not spoken about hearing voices before to any of the mental health professionals, psychiatrists, nurse practitioners, physicians and staff in the emergency department, or at McLean," Saathoff said. SIGN UP TO GET THE LATEST TRUE CRIME NEWS "This was the first time she reported that, and that she experienced an auditory hallucination, according to what she told me. So that was unusual. And then what was very unusual was the fact that the voice stopped with the strangling of her youngest son," he added. SEND US A TIP In another blow to Clancy's defense, prosecutors asked psychologist Kirk Heilbrun whether someone hearing a command hallucination could still conform their conduct to the law. WATCH: Prosecution expert says psychosis doesn't always erase knowing right from wrong GOT A TIP? "In some cases they can," he responded. LINDSAY CLANCY'S FAMILY WAS 'VERY CONCERNED' ABOUT HER MENTAL HEALTH IN THE MONTHS BEFORE SHE KILLED HER KIDS Earlier in the week, Clancy's defense called its own experts and argued she's not criminally responsible. Dr. Phillip Resnick, a forensic psychiatrist, testified that Clancy killed her children while she was experiencing a "command hallucination," stating she felt like "a puppet." It was almost like she was a puppet and someone else was pulling the strings," Resnick said. Outside the courtroom on Tuesday, one person told Fox News Digital she was there in support of Lindsay Clancy because "I've always been aware that mental health is something that's woefully in need of funding, education, all that." Obviously, a really sad story and hard to listen to at times. But if this moves the needle just a teeny tiny bit, and women start to experience more support, then I'm here for that. I was just telling my friend that when I had my children and left the hospital, nobody really said anything about postpartum, you know, be on the lookout for things. And...you know, we just had to figure it out ourselves. It shouldn't be that way. And I hope things change," the woman said.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella saw a record jump in his annual salary in 2025, a year later the signal from this annual package is clear, and it is that Microsoft Board thinks ...
articles.summary: Tech News News: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received a record total compensation package of about $96.5 million during fiscal year 2025. His latest pay package was up.
articles.body: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella received a record total compensation package of about $96.5 million during fiscal year 2025. His latest pay package was up around 22% from $79.1 million a year earlier. The increase came as Microsoft reported higher revenue, operating income and cloud growth, with the companyâs board citing âexceptional progress in artificial intelligenceâ and saying Nadellaâs leadership had positioned Microsoft as a clear AI leader amid a generational technology shift.The structure of Nadellaâs pay package also mirrors the companyâs priorities. His 2025 package was worth more than $84 million in stock awards, $2.5 million base salary and $9.5 million in cash bonuses. More than 95% of his target annual compensation is performance-based, and at least 70% of that is equity-based.The package indicates that Microsoftâs board thinks artificial intelligence (AI) and cloud growth will remain central to the companyâs performance, with Nadellaâs compensation linked to metrics that include shareholder returns, revenue and cloud growth.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadellaâs compensation rises with AI and cloud growthMicrosoftâs revenue increased roughly 15% in fiscal 2025, and operating income was up 17%. Cloud revenue rose 23% to just under $169 billion while Azure revenue increased 34% to more than $75 billion.The companyâs proxy statement links Nadellaâs compensation to the broader business performance. His performance stock awards include long-term measures such as total shareholder return compared with the S&P 500, Microsoft incentive plan revenue, Azure and other cloud services revenue, and Microsoft Cloud revenue.Nadellaâs base salary is only a small part of the total package. Most of it comes in the form of equity awards, which rise and fall with Microsoftâs stock price, so much of his compensation is linked to the companyâs future performance.Microsoft board ties Nadellaâs pay to long-term performanceMicrosoft has also structured Nadellaâs compensation around longer performance periods rather than relying on time-based stock grants. The company uses overlapping performance periods, total shareholder return modifiers and multiyear vesting for his equity awards.That means a significant portion of Nadellaâs pay is tied to Microsoftâs performance over several years. It also ties his financial results to the same elements of the business central to Microsoftâs growth strategy, such as cloud services, Azure, AI performance, and shareholder returns.Nadellaâs pay also far outpaced the median employee pay at Microsoft, as the CEO-to-median-employee pay ratio hit almost 480-to-1 in 2025. So the size of the package has attracted attention, but the structure of the package is also important for understanding how the board has linked executive pay to company performance.Microsoftâs AI strategy reflected in CEO compensationMicrosoftâs 2025 results arrived as the company kept expanding its investments in artificial intelligence and cloud infrastructure. The boardâs feedback focused on Nadella's progress on AI, even as the compensation plan continues to lean heavily on cloud and financial metrics.Nadellaâs compensation is heavily weighted to stock and performance, meaning his package is closely tied to Microsoftâs share price and business performance. âThe compensation structure is aligned with the boardâs view that AI and cloud services will be key to Microsoftâs performance going forward, while also aligning Nadellaâs financial outcome with those results.âGet the latest technology news and updates. articles.title: Video from Colombia quake falsely linked to Peru tremor
articles.summary: After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows v...
articles.body:
After a 6.7-magnitude earthquake hit southern Peru on August 20, 2026, social media posts shared a video of a crumbling structure falsely claiming it shows visuals from the tremor. The footage was in fact filmed in the Colombian city of Pereira after a 7.4-magnitude quake struck the country a week prior.

"Peru is in chaos. A powerful 7.2-magnitude earthquake has just struck the Ayacucho region in the south of the country," says a Chinese-language Douyin post shared on August 21, 2026.

The video shows the upper half of a blue building collapsing and debris falling as a man yells, "grandma, grandma...no...no" in Spanish.

A strong 6.7-magnitude earthquake struck southern Peru on August 20, US seismologists said, with authorities reporting minor injuries to three people, according to a preliminary report ( archived link ).

The Geophysical Institute of Peru (IGP) put the magnitude at 7.2 and said the quake occurred at a depth of 108 kilometres (67 miles).

In Peru, at least 22 homes, six schools and 12 medical centres have been impacted by the quake, the preliminary report found, as officials continue making damage assessments.

The tremor is the latest in a string of powerful quakes to strike South America, following deadly quakes in Venezuela on June 24 and Colombia on August 10 (archived here and here ).

Similar claims circulated across Weibo and Douyin and also spread in multiple languages such as Spanish and Japanese .

But the clip shows a quake in Colombia and not Peru.

A reverse image search on Google found an Instagram post that shared a similar photo showing the damaged blue building on August 13 ( archived link ). Its caption says Pereira.

A 7.4-magnitude tremor struck Colombia on August 10, the most powerful to hit the country in nearly half a century ( archived link ).

The quake killed nearly 300 people and destroyed more than 27,000 homes, with Pereira one of the cities affected the most ( archived link )

Google Maps street imagery of Carrera 7a in Pereira, Risaralda department, Colombia from March 2024 matches the scene in the false post ( archived link ).

Diaro del Otun, a media organisation based in Pereira, also published several photos of the same area on its Facebook account ( archived link ).

"Calle 32 at the junction of Carrera 6 and 9, Pereira...This is the state of these areas in central Pereira following the damage caused by the earthquake," the post's caption says.

AFP has debunked false claims related to recent quakes in South America.
authors: Lizeth ROMAN / Chelsea CHAN / AFP Peru / AFP Hong Kong

articles.title: âSecure, predictable sea lanes indispensableâ: India urges UN to safeguard key maritime routes
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, saying se.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India has called on the international community to work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, saying secure and predictable shipping routes are essential to ensure the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other vital commodities amid conflicts and growing disruptions to global supply chains.Speaking at a UN Security Council high-level open debate on Tuesday on the theme âFood Under Fire: The Security Council's Role in Mitigating Global and Local Food Crisesâ, Indiaâs Permanent Representative to the UN, Ambassador Harish Parvathaneni, said regional conflicts were increasingly producing consequences far beyond the immediate theatres of hostilities.âSecure and predictable maritime trade routes are indispensable for the uninterrupted movement of food, fertilisers, fuel and other essential commodities," Parvathaneni said, underscoring the need to preserve the safety and freedom of navigation for commercial shipping in accordance with international law.The call comes as conflicts and attacks on key maritime routes continue to threaten global food and energy supplies. UN secretary general Antonio Guterres told the Council that the Strait of Hormuz carries around a fifth of global oil supplies and a third of global fertiliser trade.âRestrictions and closures have driven up commodity prices and made availability plummet. And attacks on commercial vessels in the Red Sea are further threatening supply chains for food and other commodities,â Guterres said.Parvathaneni warned that disruptions to commercial shipping during conflicts could have cascading effects well beyond the affected region, with food-importing developing countries and humanitarian operations bearing a disproportionate burden.âThe international community must therefore work collectively to safeguard critical sea lanes and maritime infrastructure, while ensuring that legitimate commercial trade and humanitarian shipments are able to proceed without undue impediment,â he said.India said the immediate priority for the Security Council should be to reduce the humanitarian consequences of conflicts by facilitating safe, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access, supporting de-confliction arrangements where appropriate and ensuring that Council measures, including sanctions regimes, do not inadvertently obstruct humanitarian assistance or legitimate food and agricultural trade.Parvathaneni also called for timely assessments of disruptions to critical supply chains covering food, fertiliser, fuel and humanitarian logistics, drawing on the expertise of the food and agriculture organisation, the World Food Programme and other relevant agencies.âSuch assessments must remain objective, evidence-based and free from politicisation,â he said.The envoy said food insecurity was fundamentally a consequence of conflict, political instability and underdevelopment, rather than their root cause. He called for greater cooperation among member states, international financial institutions, regional organisations and development partners to strengthen domestic agricultural production, diversify supply chains and improve storage and logistics infrastructure.âPredictable and affordable access to fertilisers, quality seeds, technology and concessional finance remains indispensable, particularly for developing countries. Open, transparent and rules-based trade in food and agricultural inputs also remains critical to global food security,â he said.India also cautioned against âover-reliance " on any single model of production, arguing that such dependence could leave food systems vulnerable to geopolitical disruptions, economic coercion and weaponisation.âWe must encourage small and marginal farmers to enhance their productivity and contribute to ensuring food security in developing countries of the Global South. We must also encourage climate-resilient crops such as millets rather than limit conceptions of food security to the biggest staple, grain crops such as rice, wheat and corn,â Parvathaneni said.Guterres said 2025 saw the highest number of armed conflicts since World War II alongside some of the highest levels of global acute hunger on record, with at least 266 million people facing acute food insecurity.He described the simultaneous confirmation of famine in Sudan and Gaza in 2025 as a âshameful milestoneâ, adding that conflict and violence were the primary drivers of hunger in 12 of the 13 hunger hotspots of greatest concern identified in the UNâs latest Hunger Hotspots report.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Singapore sends 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes to Malaysia every week in major textile recycling partnership
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Singapore is sending up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Malaysia every week under a cross-border textile recycling partnership designed to give d.
articles.body: Singapore is sending up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Malaysia every week under a cross-border textile recycling partnership designed to give discarded garments a second life. The initiative involves social enterprise Cloop, which collects unwanted clothes through its textile recycling bins before sending them to Life Line Clothing in Port Klang, Malaysia. The volume being shipped is now twice what it was two years ago, highlighting both the growing scale of the operation and the enormous challenge of managing textile waste. At Life Line Clothingâs facility, the collected garments are sorted to determine whether they can be reused, recycled or processed into other materials. The arrangement is intended to keep more textiles in circulation and reduce the amount of clothing ultimately sent for disposal.How Singaporeâs unwanted clothes reach a recycling facility in MalaysiaThe journey begins with textile collection points across Singapore. Cloop, a social enterprise focused on textile circularity, operates recycling bins where members of the public can deposit unwanted clothing. Instead of treating these garments as ordinary household waste, the collection system channels them into a sorting and recovery process. The scale of the operation has grown substantially. According to CNA, Singapore now sends up to 70 tonnes of unwanted clothing to Life Line Clothing in Malaysia every week, around twice the amount shipped through the arrangement two years ago. The increase demonstrates how a collection network can move significant quantities of discarded textiles across borders for further processing. Once the clothing reaches Port Klang, it enters Life Line Clothingâs textile recovery operation. Garments are assessed and separated according to their condition and material, allowing usable items and recyclable textiles to follow different pathways. The cross-border model also reflects the practical challenges of textile recycling in a densely populated city. Clothing can contain blends of fibres, dyes, buttons, zips and other components that make straightforward recycling difficult. Sorting is therefore an important stage in determining whether a garment can be worn again or needs to be processed into another form.What happens to the clothes after they arrive in MalaysiaAt Life Line Clothingâs facility in Port Klang, the collected garments are sorted for reuse and recycling. The objective is to identify clothing that still has value as a wearable item while directing damaged or unsuitable textiles towards material recovery. CNA visited the Malaysian facility to examine what happens to the clothing after it leaves Singapore. Reuse is generally the simplest way to extend a garmentâs life because it keeps the existing product in circulation without requiring the fabric to be broken down and manufactured again. Clothing that cannot be reused can instead enter recycling streams, where fibres and materials may be recovered for other applications. The process illustrates why simply placing unwanted clothing into a collection bin does not necessarily mean every item will become a new garment. Textile recovery involves multiple stages, and the final destination depends heavily on the condition, composition and quality of each item. For Singapore, however, diverting clothing into a dedicated recovery system creates an opportunity to manage textiles as a resource rather than immediately treating them as waste. The growing volume being handled by the partnership suggests that more unwanted garments are entering this recovery pathway.In practice, only about half of the clothing that arrives at the facility is resold, typically compressed into bales and shipped to wholesalers in overseas secondhand markets such as Kenya, Uganda and Papua New Guinea. The remaining half is repurposed into rags or industrial wiping cloths rather than reused as garments. Items that cannot be reused or repurposed in any form are, as a last resort, incinerated to generate electricity.Why the 70-tonne weekly flow matters for textile wasteThe partnership comes against a wider challenge facing cities around the world, the environmental impact of discarded clothing. Textile production requires raw materials, water, energy and manufacturing resources, while discarded garments can represent a significant loss of those resources when they are not reused or recovered. The Singapore-Malaysia arrangement attempts to address part of this problem by extending the useful life of textiles. Sending as much as 70 tonnes of clothing each week for recovery creates a large-scale route through which garments can be sorted, reused or recycled rather than simply discarded. The fact that the volume has doubled compared with two years earlier is also significant. It could indicate that more people are using textile collection points, that larger quantities of clothing are being collected, or that the recovery partnership has expanded its capacity. Nevertheless, there is more to cutting down the wastage than merely recycling the waste. The lifespan of the fabrics can be extended through reuse and repairs and the responsible purchase of new clothes. It thus means that the process of creating a successful circular system will require not only the collection but also changes to the way in which clothes are produced, purchased, used, and discarded. One such example of an organization working to recover waste textiles is the collaboration between Cloop and Life Line Clothing. Through the transportation of 70 tonnes of unwanted clothes per week from Singapore to the processing facility in Malaysia, the project creates a huge recovery pathway for the fabrics that would have ended up as waste.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 'They had gone towards Sargodha': Ex-Navy officer backs former CDS Anil Chauhan on Kirana Hills remarks
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Former director of naval operations and intelligence commodore Ranjit Rai (Retd.) on Tuesday said former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) Gener.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former director of naval operations and intelligence commodore Ranjit Rai (Retd.) on Tuesday said former Chief of Defence Staff (CDS) General Anil Chauhan's remarks on Pakistan's Kirana Hills indicated that Operation Sindoor was a "total success", particularly highlighting India's use of loitering munitions during the 87-hour military operation.Speaking to news agency ANI, Rai was reacting to Chauhan's remarks that an Indian loitering munition deployed to search for radars in and around Sargodha in Pakistan "must have" hit an area in the Kirana Hills after failing to locate its intended target."He made it absolutely clear that it was a total success (Operation Sindoor)," Rai told ANI. He said Chauhan had made it clear that during the 87-hour operation, loitering munitions were deployed and operated around Sargodha.Rai also pointed to the significance of Kirana Hills, located around 10 kilometres north of Sargodha."He disclosed that during the operation, loitering munitions, which are drones, were used. They were loitering 10 miles from Sargodha; they had gone towards Sargodha, but 10 miles from Sargodha is the Khirana Hills. Pakistan has carried out some critical nuclear tests at the Khirana Hills. Underground in Kirana, they have got some nuclear facility. I mean, this is a revolution, telling the world about Operation Sindoor," he said.Chauhan, speaking at the Vivekananda Centre in New Delhi on Tuesday, said India had sent loitering munitions towards Sargodha to search for radars in and around the area. He explained that the weapons had a flight time of around two hours and, if they failed to locate a target during that period, would eventually come down and hit an area."I think I'll clarify this...at occasions, it's been asked whether Kirana Hills were hit or not, which is where their (Pakistan's) nuclear facilities are... Before those strikes, we had sent in a lot of loitering munitions at Sargodha and Kirana Hills is about 10 kilometres north of Sargodha. So the loitering ammunition is looking for radars which are in and around Sargodha, and it has a lifetime, which means it will loiter for about two hours and once it does not find a target, it comes down and hits somewhere," Chauhan said."It must have come and hit one of those hills. So that could be one of the reasons as to what people asked, because Pakistani media also showed some kind of images in which there was smoke coming out from Kirana Hills," he added.What Chauhan said about Kirana HillsChauhan's remarks clarified that Kirana Hills was not deliberately selected as a target during Operation Sindoor. Rather, according to his account, a loitering munition searching for radars around Sargodha may have struck one of the hills after failing to find its intended target.The comments also put his remarks in the context of an earlier statement by Air Marshal AK Bharti, who was director general of air operations during Operation Sindoor.On May 12, 2025, Bharti had rejected speculation that Indian forces had deliberately targeted Kirana Hills."Thank you for telling us that Kirana Hills houses some nuclear installations. We did not know about it. We have not hit Kirana Hills. I did not brief in my briefing yesterday," Bharti had said.Chauhan similarly referred to the earlier statement and explained that the possible impact on Kirana Hills was linked to the operation of loitering munitions sent towards Sargodha.Operation Sindoor was launched by India following the Pahalgam terror attack in which 26 people were killed.The Indian Armed Forces targeted terror infrastructure in Pakistan and Pakistan-occupied Jammu and Kashmir (PoK). As Pakistan sought to escalate the conflict, India also struck Pakistani airbases before Pakistan sought a ceasefire.Chauhan also said Prime Minister Narendra Modi had given the military "complete freedom of action" before Operation Sindoor and told the armed forces to decide the timing of the operation while ensuring there was no scope for failure.The ex-CDS had said the Prime Minister told the military to act at its own time, ensure there was no reason for failure, maintain evidence of the actions taken and exercise "complete freedom of action."Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Man seen in Philadelphia wearing creepy, Chucky-style mask is arrested in Las Vegas, authorities say
articles.summary: An arrest warrant was issued in Philadelphia after a masked man chased a jogger there and said, “Are you ready to die?” Authorities say he wanted to boost his social media views.
articles.body: A man alleged to have been seen in Philadelphia wearing a creepy, Chucky-style mask and harassing people there last week was arrested in Las Vegas, authorities in the desert city said Tuesday. Zymire Hughes was arrested by members of the U.S. Marshals Service Violent Offender Task Force, the service said in a statement. Philadelphia District Attorney Larry Krasner said last week that the warrant is based on allegations of felony and misdemeanor assault after a masked man chased a jogger, asked, “Do you want to die?” and caused her to suffer injuries as she fled early last Wednesday in Center City. He said that more charges were possible and that they would be outlined after the suspect was arrested. Booking information from the Clark County Detention Center in Nevada shows Hughes in custody with no bail, with a hearing before a judge scheduled for Thursday morning. It’s not clear whether he has legal counsel. Public defender’s offices in Clark County, Nevada, and Philadelphia did not immediately respond to requests for comment after regular business hours late Tuesday. Police allege Hughes approached more than a dozen people in Center City before he fled after his interaction with the jogger. Police said he fled again after regional transit police in a train station contacted him and told him to remove his mask. Authorities followed a trail via security cameras in the city that led to an apartment building where, they say, Hughes lives. Three people identified the masked suspect as Hughes, police said at a news conference last week. The mask resembles the killer doll from the “Child’s Play” horror movie franchise. Police believe the masked man may have behaved in this manner before, and they asked any other possible victims to come forward. A few days after the Center City incidents, Philadelphia Police Capt. Jason Smith said, police were tipped off that the suspect was alleged to have packed his bags and left the apartment. Krasner said Hughes is on probation for an unspecified crime in nearby Montgomery County. Smith said the suspect has two TikTok accounts and one Instagram account. He wore the mask to draw people to his online presence, Krasner said. “We’re not having it in this city,” Krasner said of the antics. “We are not tolerating it.”

articles.title: Iran and Oman outline plan for temporary Strait of Hormuz shipping lane; US rolls out sanctions
articles.summary: Iran and Oman outlined a joint proposal to establish a temporary shipping lane and launch a demining effort in the critical waterway. Follow for live updates.
articles.body:
• Strait of Hormuz: Iran and Oman outlined a joint proposal to establish a temporary shipping lane and launch a demining effort in the critical waterway. Iran’s deputy foreign minister said the yet-to-be-finalized deal would see the closure of a UN-authorized shipping channel that follows the coast of Oman, and that Iran vehemently opposes

• US pressure: The US Treasury Department has begun its new campaign to tighten sanctions against Iran , targeting aviation, shipping, technology, gold and digital assets such as cryptocurrency. Even though the measures target the regime, ordinary Iranians will inevitably be affected.

• Secondary sanctions: The US is also threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to cut economic ties with Iran — but has stopped short of actually imposing big new penalties.

• China’s response: Beijing says the new measures “will only further intensify tensions” and that China’s cooperation with Iran should not be disrupted. Iran claims it is “fully prepared” to counter the sanctions.

When US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent unveiled “Operation Economic Outcast,” threatening damaging new sanctions on countries that refuse to stop doing business with Iran, he didn’t name the one country that could decide its success or failure: China.

The world’s second-largest economy has long been a critical economic lifeline for Tehran , buying up the vast majority of its oil exports – worth an estimated tens of billions in US dollars last year – in addition to other trade.

Bringing it on board with the White House’s latest effort to subdue an Iranian leadership stubbornly defiant after almost six months of war, however, is an extremely tall order.

Beijing flatly rejects what it calls “unilateral” US sanctions and has long defended its right to regular trade with partners like Iran and Russia. It also surmises that Washington would be wary of triggering a broader economic confrontation that would hurt both countries, right ahead of the US midterms.

On Tuesday, following Bessent’s press conference, China’s Foreign Ministry vowed to “take all necessary measures” to safeguard its “own legitimate rights and interests” in the face of US sanction threats.

“Economic warfare and maximum pressure will not help resolve the issue; they will only further intensify tensions and conflicts, create spillover risks, disrupt the global economic and financial order,” ministry spokesperson Lin Jian said.

Bessent’s threat also comes ahead of a highly anticipated visit by Chinese leader Xi Jinping to the US next month, where the two sides could make progress on extending a critical trade truce set to expire later this fall.

A key route currently used by ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz would close under a pending Iran-Oman deal, according to a senior Iranian diplomat.

After weeks of fraught discussions , Tehran and Muscat outlined a proposal Tuesday to jointly establish a temporary shipping channel through the strait, and to “clear mines.”

Iran’s Deputy Foreign Minister Kazem Gharibabadi later said the yet-to-be-finalized deal would see the closure of the southern route, a UN-authorized shipping channel that follows the coast of Oman and that Iran vehemently opposes, state-linked Press TV reported.

The earlier Omani statement did not mention the route’s closure.

In recent weeks, the US government and ship tracking organizations have noted a growing amount of oil is transiting the critical waterway, despite Iran’s insistence it is closed. Much of that is traveling via the Omani route – or has taken that route as “dark” transits, during which ships turn off their tracking transponders, CNN reported last week.

While Iran has attacked dozens of ships that attempted to travel the southern route, many ships have recently chosen to ignore Iran’s demands and cross the strait with the promise of protection from US naval forces.

Gharibabadi said the potential new joint route agreed with Oman would see vessels “pass through Iranian waters in both directions,” the Press TV report said.

But whether the US, which insists the strait is international waters, would accept the new route is unclear. Last week, President Donald Trump threatened to attack Oman if it interfered with US efforts in the waterway.

Washington has worked to undermine Tehran’s claims of control of the strait, warning shipping firms on Monday they could face sanctions or penalties even if they comply with information requests from Iranian agencies over transits.

Iran and Oman outlined a proposal Tuesday to jointly establish a temporary shipping channel through the Strait of Hormuz, according to regional officials, after weeks of fraught discussions between the two countries.

Tehran and Muscat discussed a “phased framework” for a joint project facilitating a “temporary shipping corridor” and to “clear mines,” a press statement from the Iranian and Omani foreign ministries said.

Officials will carry on talks “with the aim of reaching agreement on a permanent shipping corridor and the future administration of the Strait,” the statement added.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr bin Hamad Al Busaidi visited Iran and held consultations with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi, the state-run Oman News Agency (ONA) reported earlier.

After the meeting, the Omani foreign minister said he was “hopeful” both nations would “soon announce a temporary corridor” for the strait. “Future management of the Strait and a permanent solution will follow in due course,” he posted on X . “Discussions with regional partners will be conducted in support of peace and cooperation, stability and freedom of navigation,” Al Busaidi added.

Araghchi wrote in a post on X that the proposed deal showed that “Iran’s commitment to peace and stability is matched by steadfast diplomacy with our neighbors.”

Over the past few weeks, Tehran and Muscat held negotiations to stabilize shipping in the waterway, which has emerged as a key bargaining chip in stalled discussions between Iran and the US, following months of regional violence.

Earlier today, US President Donald Trump reiterated that all mines in the Strait of Hormuz have been removed or detonated , and he threatened to destroy any boats that try to place more. “We are watching every square inch of the strait,” he said.

Meanwhile, Qatar Prime Minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al-Thani and Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi held a telephone call and discussed the proposed temporary shipping channel, the Qatar foreign ministry said Tuesday.

Qatar has previously voiced support for the efforts between Oman and Iran to reach an agreement over the Strait of Hormuz, despite US President Donald Trump’s threat to attack Oman if it interferes with US operations in the strategic waterway.

A sweeping new US sanctions campaign targeting Iran and its economic partners is drawing criticism from China and defiance from Tehran, with senior Iranian officials vowing Washington’s economic pressure will fail.

Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf claimed Tuesday that after suffering defeat “in the military and political war,” the United States “will also be defeated in its economic actions,” according to Iran’s semi-official Tasnim News Agency.

Here’s a look at what’s in the new measures under the Trump administration’s “Operation Economic Outcast,” a campaign Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent described as an effort to “sever every economic lifeline” sustaining Iran’s government.

Sanctions on more than 60 targets: According to Bessent, the Treasury Department’s Office of Foreign Assets Control is sanctioning “over 60 entities, individuals, and vessels across the world” accused of helping Iran procure nuclear and missile technology, conduct cyber operations and generate oil revenue.

Five sectors targeted : The administration announced new sanctions determinations covering five sectors that Washington views as critical to Iran’s economy: digital assets, technology, gold, aviation and shipping. Bessent said the measures increase the risk of sanctions for foreign companies and individuals that continue doing business with Iran in those sectors.

Pressure on countries dealing with Iran : The treasury secretary said US officials are meeting governments worldwide and informing them that Washington expects action against economic activities linked to Iran. “Every country has a defined timeline to shut down activities we have identified,” Bessent said. “If they do not take action, we will do so unilaterally through Treasury authorities.”

Iranian financial networks in focus: Bessent specifically singled out Iran’s Bank Melli, saying: “Every Bank Melli branch must be shuttered.” He also warned that entities facilitating money laundering on behalf of Iran could lose access to the US dollar system.

Oil exports and sanctions evasion: The treasury secretary said Washington has mapped Iran’s networks used to “smuggle oil and evade sanctions” and pledged a “zero-leakage approach” to cut off revenue streams that fund the Iranian government and the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps.

articles.title: More than a dozen infants killed in hospital fire in Pakistan’s capital
articles.summary: At least 13 children, mostly newborns, have died after a fire broke out at the gynecology ward of the largest hospital in Pakistan’s capital, police told CNN.
articles.body: At least 13 children, mostly newborns, have died after a fire broke out at the gynecology ward of the largest hospital in Pakistan’s capital, police told CNN. The fire broke out in a nursery for newborn babies at the Pakistan Institute for Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad, the sources said. The blaze appears to have been triggered by an air conditioning compressor explosion inside the nursery, according to rescue sources. Hospital authorities were able to rescue one child, the sources said. The blaze has also left some babies in critical condition and the death toll could rise, they added. Islamabad’s Chief Commissioner Sohail Ashraf said an emergency fire call was made just before 7 a.m. local time Wednesday. Rescue teams rushed to the scene and “controlled the fire,” Ashraf said in a post to X. The government-run PIMS facility is located on a sprawling site in the capital. According to its website, its mission is “to be a premier research-intensive medical university that will educate medical students, paramedics, and postdoctoral fellows in accordance with international professional standards.” Hospital fires are not uncommon in Pakistan, especially in government hospitals which often run on outdated electrical systems.

articles.title: â3,000 raids, dirty kitchens exposed, food giants hitâ: How Tukaram Mundhe is giving eateries a wake-up call
articles.summary: MUMBAI: \"I don't think I'm a celebrity. I'm just a food safety commissioner,\" Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters as his crackdown on unhygienic food business.
articles.body: MUMBAI: "I don't think I'm a celebrity. I'm just a food safety commissioner," Tukaram Mundhe told Reuters as his crackdown on unhygienic food businesses across Mumbai has struck a chord with the public.Since taking charge as Maharashtra's food safety chief in May, Mundhe's teams have conducted more than 3,000 raids, suspended permits at several outlets of major food chains and uncovered alleged violations ranging from poor hygiene to expired food and pest infestations.A crackdownMundhe's teams have targeted major food chains as well as local restaurants, roadside vendors, hotels and long-established establishments.The commissioner has led the suspension of permits at four Domino's and one Pizza Hut outlet in recent weeks.When a Mumbai judge questioned whether Mundhe's department was selectively targeting private businesses and asked whether court canteens had been inspected, his teams carried out inspections there within hours and shut some operating without licences."Those who try to not comply, they will face what is expected from the regulator," Mundhe said in an interview with Reuters."You are dealing with the lives of people."Rats, cockroaches and expired foodImages released after the raids have shown alleged violations including stained walls, cockroaches, rats and expired food at eateries and food-storage facilities."It was surprising. I did not expect these many violations," Mundhe told Reuters.Reuters visits to 25 street vendors and restaurants in Mumbai found that some businesses had changed their practices amid heightened scrutiny.One vendor had replaced artificial red dye with natural chilli, while another had started changing its frying oil three times a day and requiring staff to wear gloves and head caps.Mundhe has also prohibited the use of newspapers to wrap Mumbai's popular vada pav, citing food safety concerns.'Giving people hope'Mundhe's actions have earned him a following among members of the public frustrated by longstanding concerns about food hygiene."Everyone has tried to normalise this for years by saying it happens in India. It's basically bottled-up anger," said Ankur Bisen, a partner at consumer consulting firm The Knowledge Company."I have never seen anyone like Mundhe. It's giving people hope."But businesses have accused his department of being heavy-handed, with some approaching the High Court.In one case, judges fined the department Rs 5 lakh for continuing to suspend an eatery after it had improved its compliance."If there are observations by the court, we take it seriously. If there is scope for improvement, we improve," Mundhe told Reuters.Why the FDA is targeting loose edible oil'The food safety drive has now expanded to the sale of loose edible oil, prompting concern among traditional traders and small retailers.The Maharashtra Food and Drug Administration (FDA) says the move is not a new restriction but an enforcement of food safety provisions that have been in force since 2011.The FDA said edible oil sold directly to consumers must be supplied in sealed, tamper-evident and properly labelled packaging under existing food safety regulations.Mundhe said the requirement was intended to make businesses accountable and allow consumers to trace the source, batch and age of the oil.The department said oil sold directly from drums, tanks, cans or tankers into containers brought by customers, or transferred into smaller containers after the original seal is broken, falls under loose or unauthorised repacking.Bulk movement of edible oil by licensed businesses for manufacturing or transportation is allowed under prescribed rules, the FDA said.But oil sold to the final consumer must be in sealed and labelled packaging.FDA warns of adulterationThe department said loose oil often lacks information about the manufacturer, packer, batch number, date and source.That makes it difficult to trace the product or establish responsibility if a consumer falls ill or a food safety problem is detected.The FDA also warned that loose sales can make adulteration easier, including mixing cheaper oil with expensive varieties or selling one type of oil as another.It said exposure to air, heat and light could increase the risk of oxidation and rancidity, while unclean or reused containers could introduce dust, water, insects, metal particles or chemical residues into the oil.The absence of manufacturing, packing and 'Best Before' dates also makes it difficult to determine the age of the product, the department said.Traders raise concernThe crackdown has triggered concern among traditional oil traders and small retailers who fear that mandatory packaging could increase costs and affect their businesses.Chief minister Devendra Fadnavis said the FDA would be asked to prepare standard operating procedures to prevent adulteration without crippling the businesses of traditional oil traders and small retailers.The FDA said consumers would still be able to buy oil in small quantities through packaged products.It pointed to 200 ml, 500 ml and one-litre packs, particularly pouches, which it described as among the least expensive packaging options.Rule has been in place for yearsThe FDA said Maharashtra had previously allowed temporary exemptions for the sale of loose edible oil.The last such extension ended in 2020 and did not amount to permanent permission, it said.After the exemption expired, food businesses were required to comply with the original restriction under Regulation 2.3.15.The department said the provision was introduced as a food safety measure following serious incidents such as epidemic dropsy.It said packaging and labelling were necessary to prevent adulteration, establish producer responsibility, trace batches and enable recalls.More than Rs 5 crore worth of oil seizedThe FDA collected 1,247 edible oil samples across Maharashtra during 2025-26.Of these, 1,142 met prescribed standards, while 77 were found substandard, 13 unsafe and 15 misbranded.The department also seized 3,20,781 kg of edible oil worth around Rs 5.31 crore.In Beed district alone, loose edible oil worth about Rs 1.94 crore was confiscated.The FDA said the rules apply across India and cited an FSSAI special drive in August 2022, when more than 27,500 litres of loose edible oil were seized across states and Union articles.title: Scientists found a 4-million-year-old baby tapir in Spain, the most complete juvenile skeleton of its kind ever found in Europe
articles.summary: Europe News: At the Camp dels Ninots site in Caldes de Malavella, near Girona in northeastern Spain, researchers have recovered a remarkably complete skeleton of a.
articles.body: At the Camp dels Ninots site in Caldes de Malavella, near Girona in northeastern Spain, researchers have recovered a remarkably complete skeleton of a young tapir that died roughly 4 million years ago, when the region was still home to a humid subtropical landscape surrounding an ancient volcanic lake. The animal, estimated to have been about 1 year old, belongs to Tapirus arvernensis, an extinct species that lived across parts of Europe during the Pliocene. Its bones were found largely connected in their original anatomical positions, preserving an unusually detailed record of a juvenile animal that would otherwise be extremely difficult to study. Researchers from the Catalan Institute of Human Palaeoecology and Social Evolution, or IPHES-CERCA, say the specimen is the most complete juvenile tapir skeleton ever recovered in Europe. The discovery also brings the number of tapir individuals found at Camp dels Ninots to 7, making the site an exceptionally important record of this extinct European mammal.Why Camp dels Ninots has become a major site for studying ancient tapirsAccording to IPHES-CERCA, the Camp dels Ninots excavation has produced an unusually large number of Tapirus arvernensis remains, including individuals representing different ages and sexes. The newly recovered juvenile is particularly valuable because complete young skeletons are rare in the fossil record. Dr Bruno Gómez de Soler, an IPHES-CERCA researcher and co-director of the excavation, said the find provides an opportunity to study skeletal development, growth and other aspects of early life that are difficult to reconstruct from isolated fossil bones. Having several individuals from the same species and site also gives researchers an unusual opportunity to compare animals at different stages of development rather than relying on specimens recovered from unrelated locations.How an ancient volcanic lake preserved the tapir skeletons so wellCamp dels Ninots formed within a volcanic crater known as a maar, which later filled with water and became a lake during the Pliocene. Fine sediments accumulated on the lake floor over time, creating conditions that could rapidly bury animal remains and protect them from the processes that normally destroy fossil skeletons. That helps explain why the site has yielded exceptionally well-preserved animals, including tapirs whose bones remain in close anatomical association. Researchers have proposed that volcanic activity and gases released around the crater may have contributed to sudden animal deaths, although the precise circumstances surrounding individual specimens remain an area of investigation. The surrounding environment was also very different from modern northeastern Spain, with plant remains indicating a warmer, wetter landscape and dense vegetation around the ancient lake.What the juvenile tapir can reveal about how the species grewThe juvenile skeleton gives researchers something adult specimens cannot: a direct record of a developing Tapirus arvernensis. Young animals are particularly difficult to preserve because their developing bones are more vulnerable to destruction, scattering and scavenging before burial. Because Camp dels Ninots has produced tapirs of different ages, researchers can compare skeletal features across the population and begin reconstructing how these animals changed as they matured. The specimen will undergo further laboratory analysis after excavation, including detailed recording of the bones and examination of the surrounding sediment. Researchers hope those studies will clarify aspects of the animal's development while also revealing more about the conditions that allowed its skeleton to survive for approximately 4 million years.Why 7 tapirs from one site matter to palaeontologistsThe latest discovery strengthens Camp dels Ninots' importance as a reference site for understanding Europe's Pliocene tapirs. Tapirus arvernensis was one of the tapir species that inhabited Europe before the animals eventually disappeared from the continent, leaving their modern relatives restricted mainly to Asia and the Americas. Finding multiple individuals from one exceptionally preserved environment allows researchers to study not only individual animals but also variation within a single population. The combination of adults and juveniles is especially significant because it provides a rare opportunity to investigate growth and life history using fossils from the same geological setting. Rather than being simply another isolated prehistoric skeleton, the newly recovered tapir adds another piece to an unusually detailed record of an extinct animal and the environment in which it lived.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Lok Sabha Speaker seeks response from 20 rebel TMC MPs on disqualification petitions
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who are now affiliated with the little-known Nationa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla has issued notices to 20 rebel Trinamool Congress (TMC) MPs who are now affiliated with the little-known Nationalist Citizens Party of India (NCPI), seeking their responses within seven days to disqualification petitions filed by the TMC.The disqualification petitions are currently pending before Birla.This comes after Solicitor General of India Tushar Mehta on Tuesday informed the Supreme Court that the Speaker had already issued notices to the 20 MPs on the disqualification petitions filed by the TMC under the Tenth Schedule of the Constitution.Mehta made the submission before a bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant while appearing for the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House. The bench was hearing a plea filed by senior TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee, challenging the delay in deciding the petitions seeking the disqualification of the rebels.Responding to the submission, the bench said, "It is not a question of issuing notices, it is a question of concluding the proceedings within a time frame."During the hearing, the bench indicated that it was inclined to issue notices to the respondents on Abhishek Banerjeeâs writ petition. Mehta, however, submitted that there was no need to issue notices to the Speaker or his office, stating that he would appear on behalf of Birla.The TMC has accused the 20 MPs of âabandoningâ the party and subsequently joining the NCPI. Abhishek Banerjee has contended that their conduct attracts disqualification under the anti-defection provisions of the Constitution.The petition names the Lok Sabha Speaker and the Secretary General of the House as the principal respondents and also impleads the MPs whose disqualification is being sought.The respondents are Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar, Sudip Bandyopadhyay, Satabdi Roy, Prasun Banerjee, Rachana Banerjee, Jagadish Chandra Barma Basunia, Partha Bhowmick, Arup Chakraborty, Adhikari Deepak Dev, Sayani Ghosh, Bapi Haldar, Md Abu Taher Khan, Kalipada Saren Kherwal, Asit Kumar Mal, June Maliah, Mitali Bag, Khalilur Rahaman, Mala Roy, Sharmila Sarkar and Yusuf Pathan.(With ANI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Donald Trump sends Saudi civil nuclear deal to Congress, keeps Israel normalisation as condition
articles.summary: US News: US President Donald Trumpâs administration has submitted a proposed civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, whil.
articles.body: US President Donald Trumpâs administration has submitted a proposed civil nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia to Congress for review, while maintaining that the pact will only move forward if Riyadh agrees to normalise relations with Israel.The agreement was sent to Congress on Monday under the requirements of the US Atomic Energy Act, according to an administration official cited by Reuters.The Wall Street Journal first reported the formal submission.The agreement was signed last month in Washington by US energy secretary Chris Wright and Saudi energy minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman. It would allow US companies to play a central role in developing Saudi Arabiaâs civilian nuclear programme.A US administration official told Reuters that Trumpâs position had not changed and that the agreement would only take effect if Saudi Arabia joins the Abraham Accords, the US-brokered framework for normalising relations between Israel and Arab and Muslim-majority countries.Trump had linked the nuclear deal to normalisation shortly after the agreement was reached. On July 23, he said the civil nuclear deal would be approved but was âtotally subject to Saudi Arabia joining the very respected and successful Abraham Accordsâ.Congress gets 90 days to review nuclear pactUnder US law, Congress has 90 days while in session to review the agreement. Unless lawmakers pass a joint resolution rejecting it during that period, the pact can take effect without a separate vote by either chamber.According to AP, the submission was made to Capitol Hill on Monday.The proposed pact is expected to last 30 years. It would facilitate the development of Saudi Arabiaâs nuclear infrastructure using US technology, including AP1000 reactors.The project could involve US firms in the construction and development of the programme following a joint US-Saudi study.The agreement has also drawn scrutiny over nuclear non-proliferation. Some Democratic lawmakers and non-proliferation advocates have criticised the pact because it does not bar Saudi Arabia from enriching uranium or reprocessing nuclear waste, which can provide potential pathways towards producing nuclear weapons.The United Arab Emirates accepted restrictions on enrichment and reprocessing, known as the âgold standardâ, in its 2009 civil nuclear agreement with the US.The Trump administration has said the Saudi agreement contains the non-proliferation measures required under US law.Saudi-Israel normalisation remains key hurdleTrumpâs condition could complicate the agreementâs path forward because Saudi Arabia has maintained that it would only establish diplomatic relations with Israel if there is a clear and irreversible path towards Palestinian statehood.Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has rejected Palestinian statehood, saying it would be untenable for Israelâs security.The Abraham Accords, reached in 2020 and 2021, established diplomatic relations between Israel and the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Morocco and Sudan. Saudi Arabia has so far not joined the framework.Trumpâs administration has nevertheless continued to pursue an expansion of the accords, while Riyadh has maintained its position on Palestinian statehood.The proposed nuclear agreement has also faced criticism in the US over its potential implications for nuclear proliferation in West Asia.Henry Sokolski, head of the Nonproliferation Policy Education Centre, told Reuters that beginning the congressional review could allow the deal to proceed without some of the restrictions sought by its critics.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Who was the woman who placed her hands on President Murmuâs shoulders at the Padma Awards? Meet Hirbai Ibrahim Lobi, the Siddi social worker who changed more than 700 lives
articles.summary: A quiet moment from the 2023 Padma Awards continues to draw attention. As she received the Padma Shri from President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bha.
articles.body: A quiet moment from the 2023 Padma Awards continues to draw attention. As she received the Padma Shri from President Droupadi Murmu at Rashtrapati Bhavan, social worker Hirbai Ibrahim Lobi did something that stood out amid the formality of the ceremony- she reached out and affectionately placed her hands on the Presidentâs shoulders.The gesture was warm and spontaneous, and captured something of Lobiâs personality: a woman who had spent much of her life working at the grassroots and speaking for a community that has often remained outside the national spotlight. But who was Hirbai Ibrahim Lobi?Hirbai Ibrahim Lobi was a social worker from Jambur village in Gujarat's Gir Somnath district and a prominent member of the Siddi community, a small African-origin community that has lived in parts of India for centuries.She dedicated much of her life to improving the lives of Siddi women and children, particularly through education, financial independence, employment and better farming practices. Her work eventually earned her the Padma Shri in 2023 for social work.Lobi's own childhood was far removed from privilege. She lost her parents at a young age and was raised by her grandmother. Hirbai was married at the age of 14. She did not receive formal education, yet education remained one of the central themes of her life's work.She learned from the radio- and passed that knowledge onOne of the most remarkable parts of Lobi's story is how she educated herself. Without access to formal schooling, she turned to the radio. Programmes about agriculture, government schemes and women's development became an informal classroom for her. She would listen, learn and then share what she had learnt with other women in her community.Her interest in organic farming, for instance, began after she heard about techniques for making organic fertilizer on the radio. She later used that knowledge in her own community.Her work was especially significant because many Siddi women in the area depended on cutting wood for their livelihoods, sometimes working in areas around the Gir forest. Lobi worked to help women find alternative sources of income and become financially independent.From opening bank accounts to creating employmentLobi's work was not limited to awareness campaigns. She helped Siddi women understand banking and savings, encouraged them to become economically independent and worked with social organisations to create employment opportunities. More than 700 women were reported to have benefited from her efforts.She also worked to improve children's access to education and helped establish balwadis, or early-childhood learning centres, in the community.In 2004, she founded the Mahila Vikas Foundation, which became an important part of her work towards women's empowerment. The governmentâs Padma citation also notes that she was associated with the Adivasi Mahila Sangh, also known as the Siddi Women's Federation.Her approach was simple: learn something useful and make sure others could benefit from it too.The Padma Awards ceremony in March 2023 produced another memorable moment involving Lobi. As she walked towards the stage to receive her award, she stopped near Prime Minister Narendra Modi, who was seated in the front row with other Union ministers. Rather than simply walking past, she spoke about what the honour meant to her community.She told him that her community had lived in the forests and often remained unnoticed, describing the Padma Shri as an honour they had never imagined receiving. PM Modi responded by bowing his head and greeting her with folded hands. The exchange was followed by applause from those present at the ceremony.And then came the moment with President MurmuAfter speaking to the Prime Minister, Lobi went on to receive the Padma Shri from President Droupadi Murmu. And the viral moment happened. Lobi affectionately placed her hands on Murmu's shoulders. Once the award was given to her by the President, she again happily placed her hands on President Murmuâs shoulder. Her happiness could be seen through her eyes.Lobi's gesture appeared to carry the warmth and informality of someone meeting another woman from a similar social world, rather than treating the occasion only as a formal exchange between an award recipient and the country's President.A life built around her communityHirbai Ibrahim Lobi died at her home in Jambur village on January 24, 2025, at the age of 65. She was survived by two sons and a daughter. Her death was mourned as a major loss for the Siddi community.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.title: Practical Magic 2's Kidman and Bullock board Essex vintage train
articles.summary: The stars appear on the train, specially transported to a film studos for a new movie sequel.
articles.body:
A call from Hollywood producers asking if film stars Nicole Kidman and Sandra Bullock could sit in a vintage railway carriage came out of the blue for station manager Robert Bentley.

They called him to ask if the duo could use it for their new blockbuster, Practical Magic 2, a sequel to the 1998 romantic fantasy tale.

While film producers were keen to feature it, they first needed the train moved from North Weald, Essex, to the Warner Bros Studios in Leavesden, Hertfordshire.

The studio filming left Bentley "in awe", he said. "When you're stood at the studio and then all of a sudden Sandra is stood next to you, it's hard to describe the feeling."

The 27-year-old said he ended up chatting to Bullock, who was interested in the history of the train.

Epping Ongar Railway has preserved its stations and carriages since closing in the 1990s.

Its authentic appearance has made it a popular go-to spot for film-makers, with it appearing in the TV shows Man vs Baby and Death in Paradise in recent times.

Bentley said producers had scouted around for locations before choosing to use North Weald station for a scene with US actress Joey King, as well as its train carriage, for filming last summer.

The final choice for Bullock's scene was a 1960s British Rail Mark 1 coach.

"We were the perfect fit for them in terms of what they wanted to film," said Bentley.

"We had the countryside and we had the coach that they wanted."

He said payment was not six digits, but "quite a high figure".

The film-makers also asked him to stick around for a scene, casting him as the train guard with a line of dialogue.

Other scenes were filmed at St Mary and All Saints Church in Lambourne, near Abridge.

The Grade I-listed church dates back to the 12th Century, but producers felt it could pass for a US church.

Last year, it was reported film and TV shows being made in Essex generated £3m for the local economy since 2022.

The Daniel Craig thriller Wake Up Dead Man: A Knives Out Mystery - filmed at a church in Epping Forest - has been among the productions providing a boost.

Essex County Council established the Essex Film Office in 2022 to attract more large film productions to the county.

It provides a point of contact for production companies looking for perfect filming locations - guiding them in the right direction and assisting them with permissions.

Manager Erica Gilson recalled feeling "hugely proud" to work on Mr Bates vs The Post Office, which included scenes at Shire Hall in Chelmsford.

She was emotional as she spoke about the impact it had.

"You're a tiny, tiny part in something that ends up having a huge difference, and that's the power of the arts," she said.

Jeff Bray, the council's cabinet member for regeneration, planning and heritage, said the county has "so much to offer" film studios.

"We've got everything: wide open countryside, fantastic beaches, heritage of every kind from Roman through to Medieval - whatever you want you'll find it here in Essex," he said.
